'''Yashwant Singh''' (born 28 July 1944) is an Indian theoretical physicist known for his contributions to soft matter physics. He is at present Distinguished Professor and INSA Senior Scientist at [[Banaras Hindu University]].

== Biography ==
Dr. Yashwant Singh born on 28 July 1944 in a village near Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. He completed his B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Physics from [[Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University|Gorakhpur University]] (Now DDU University) in 1962 and 1964. He then joined [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science|Indian Association for the Cultivation of Sciences (IACS)]], Jadavpur, Kolkata, where he worked on transport phenomenon in  gaseous state and obtained D. Phil. from [[University of Calcutta|Calcutta University]] (1969). He started his professional career as lecturer at [[Banaras Hindu University]] where he continues to work as a Distinguished Professor. In between he has worked at [[IBM Research Laboratory|IBM Research Laboratory, California]] (1976–78).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Abraham |first1=F. F. |last2=Singh |first2=Y. |title=The structure of a hard‐sphere fluid in contact with a soft repulsive wall |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1977 |volume=67 |issue=5 |page=2384 |doi=10.1063/1.435080 }}</ref> and [[University of Illinois]], [[Urbana Champaign]] (1982–84) [[United States]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chandler |first1=D |last2=Singh |first2=Y. |title=Excess electrons in simple fluids. I. General equilibrium theory for classical hard sphere solvents |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1984 |volume=81 |issue=4 |page=1975 |doi=10.1063/1.447820 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Y. |last2=Stoessel |first2=J.P. |last3=Wolynes |first3=P.G. |title=Hard-Sphere Glass and the Density-Functional Theory of Aperiodic Crystals |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=1985 |volume=54 |issue=10 |pages=1059–1062 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.1059 |pmid=10030918 }}</ref>

Singh has made contributions to the theory of [[liquids]], [[liquid crystals]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Y. |title=Density-functional theory of freezing and properties of the ordered phase |journal=Physics Reports |date=1991 |volume=207 |issue=6 |pages=351–446 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(91)90097-6 }}</ref> [[polymer]] statistics,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mishra |first1=P.K. |last2=Kumar |first2=S. |last3=Singh |first3=Y. |title=Force-induced desorption of a linear polymer chain adsorbed on an attractive surface |journal=EPL (Europhysics Letters) |date=2005 |volume=69 |page=102 |url=http://stacks.iop.org/0295-5075/69/i=1/a=102|doi=10.1209/epl/i2004-10304-5 |arxiv=cond-mat/0404191 |s2cid=119093167 }}</ref> and to the theory of liquid-solid and solid-solid transitions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bharadwaj |first1=A.S. |last2=Singh |first2=Y. |title=Density-functional theory for fluid-solid and solid-solid phase transitions |journal=Phys. Rev. E |date=2017 |volume=95 |issue=3 |article-number=032120 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.95.032120 |pmid=28415240 }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
He is an elected Fellow of [[Indian Academy of Sciences|Indian Academy of Sciences, Bangalore]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Directory of Fellows, IAS (Bangalore) Vol. 2, 2009. |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Singh,_Prof._Yashwant}}</ref> [[The National Academy of Sciences, India]] and The [[Indian National Science Academy|Indian National Science Academy, New Delhi]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Biographical Notes, A platinum Jubilee Publication, INSA (New Delhi) Vol. II, 2009 |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/index.php}}</ref>
